channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Contest to Succeed ECB Head Lagarde Is Officially a Two-Horse Race
item.description: European governments are set to choose between two candidates to succeed Christine Lagarde: Spain’s Pablo Hernandez de Cos and the Netherlands’ Klaas Knot.

item.title: What’s Next for Iran Peace Talks After the Midterms
item.description: Elections in the U.S. and Israel have scrambled the political calculus in both countries, as Qatar makes a fresh push to mediate.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of November 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: Taiwan Activates Market-Stabilization Measures to Stem AI Bleeding
item.description: Taiwanese authorities joined South Korea in moving to stem the bleeding in local equities caused by the global selloff in artificial intelligence-related stocks.

item.title: Israel’s Most Important Alliance Is Confronting Its Biggest Test in Decades
item.description: Democratic wins and shifting signals from the White House point to change in Israel’s most crucial relationship.

item.title: To Cross the Red Sea, Shippers Email Houthi Rebels. Read Their Inbox.
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reviewed the correspondence between shippers and the Yemeni militant group’s little-known clearance office.

item.title: Moscow Seizes Japan Tobacco’s Russia Factories
item.description: The move follows a Russian pattern of targeting Western firms over Ukraine and punishing Tokyo.

item.title: Gulf Airports Built to Connect the World Are Now in the Crosshairs
item.description: The region’s renowned aviation hubs are a few hours from much of the world’s population, but even closer to Iran’s missiles.

item.title: A Soldier Cut Off His Own Foot to Survive. Then Came a Daring Drone Rescue.
item.description: Pvt. Vlasenko was alone and injured on the front line—a human trapped in a robot war. Saving him would require a new solution.

item.title: Colombia Arrests Mexican Judge Tied to Drug Gang Led by Ex-Olympian
item.description: The U.S. wanted judge Luis Benítez on charges that he took a $2 million bribe to release a top Canadian drug boss.

item.title: Paraguay’s President Resigns as Collapse of Bank With Close Ties to Him Sparks Crisis
item.description: Santiago Peña’s downfall rattled a fast-growing South American economy that has attracted investors and forged close ties with the U.S.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Has No Easy Choices as It Weighs How to Combat Houthi Threat
item.description: The kingdom asked the Iran-backed militants what it would take to make peace. The response: $51 billion.

item.title: Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape, Sexual Assault Charges
item.description: The verdict follows a four-week trial in London. The sentencing will occur Monday.

item.title: Bomb Threats Cause Diverted Flights, Emergency Landings Across Europe
item.description: More than a dozen flights have been affected, with Rome’s main airport receiving an email threat purporting to be from a fringe ultranationalist Russian group.

item.title: Bank of England Raises Rates for First Time Since Start of Iran War
item.description: The conflict has lifted energy prices, though they have fallen since the midterms raised hopes for an end to the war.

item.title: China Blocks $5.4 Billion SoftBank Robot Deal, Flexing Control Over AI Tech
item.description: Beijing is seeking to keep AI data and expertise developed at home from leaking abroad.

item.title: How Trump’s War in Iran and Missteps Flipped Washington Overnight
item.description: Plus, billions of dollars in orders are complicating an end to U.S. aid to Israel, and the blue wave sets off a potential regime change in markets.

item.title: The Hanoi Lake Where Kids Hustle American Tourists for English Lessons
item.description: Squads of children looking to become fluent hunt down foreigners to be their living, breathing Duolingo lessons.

item.title: ArcelorMittal Says Europe’s Steel Tariffs Are Boosting Profits
item.description: Europe’s largest steelmaker booked a 34% surge in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization over the third quarter of the year.

item.title: Hong Kong Extends Jailed Activist Joshua Wong’s Prison Term by 10 Years
item.description: Rights groups say a security law was used as a political weapon against the 30-year-old protest leader.
